summary: Clay County, KY tower in Daniel Boone NF; a 1941 item ties it to the renamed Icy Cliff tower, a 1950 survey describes an 80-ft steel tower, and NHLR registered it in 2026.

facts.design: Four-legged steel structure with an observation room painted gray (1950 survey description)
facts.agency: Forest Service, Daniel Boone National Forest (presumed)

events.note: Renamed the John William Bell Tower; the Register quotes a 1941 Somerset newspaper item calling the Clay County tower the Icy Cliff lookout tower
Coast and Geodetic Survey described a station at the center of the tower base in 1950; the tower is an 80-ft four-legged steel structure
Present on the 1954 USGS Beverly, KY quadrangle (field checked 1954)
Listed as standing per Google Earth imagery dated April 4, 2023
Registered June 28, 2026; nominated by Tyler Helton

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register says the build year is unknown. The Coast and Geodetic Survey designation reads Bell Lookout Tower 1950, which may be a survey date rather than a build year. The 1941 renaming item suggests a tower already existed by 1941, but no source confirms it is this structure.

notes_for_editor: Medium confidence. The Register and the Forest Lookouts page (quoting a 1950 Coast and Geodetic Survey description) agree on location and steel-tower form. The 1941 Icy Cliff renaming is known only from the Register's quotation of The Commonwealth (Somerset, KY, Oct. 15, 1941); the newspaper itself was not read, and the Register files it under this entry without saying it describes the same structure. The NGS datasheet was not fetched directly. The rough-condition line in the Register is undated. Two searches for the tower's history and for John William Bell found nothing usable. No staffing, access, fire or visit data in any source. Not verified: condition after the April 2023 imagery. No photo captured.
